actual_tool_job.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Produce one corrected complete portrait card. Image 1 is the exact rejected full-resolution generated PNG to edit; Image 2 is the exact unchanged original game card, the sole composition/clothing/hair/pose authority; Image 3 is the user mascot identity only. Correct the documented visual defects in Image 1 using Image 2, and retain all already correct parts.
REQUIRED SOURCE-SPECIFIC REPAIR: Correct the clearly wrong head direction and garment collar: Image 2 is nearly frontal with only a slight IMAGE-RIGHT turn; change Image 1 away from its current image-left three-quarter view. Keep both eyes almost equal in apparent size. Retain the source swept-back dark hair and visible eyebrow hair. Reproduce Image 2 blue-grey CLOSED HIGH tunic collar and central fastening, replacing the invented wide pointed folded collar. Serious closed mascot mouth, no added facial hair. Preserve existing opaque frame/backing/note and original crop.
Retain the recognizable smooth golden-yellow compact rounded mascot head, green-ringed black eyes and small closed mascot mouth. Preserve source hairstyle, eyebrow HAIR and any facial hair precisely where visible; a bare reference scalp must not erase them. Keep original lighting, pose, garment design/fastening, photo-frame angle, opaque grey backing and overlapping cream note with faint indistinct upper marks. Do not infer appearance from filenames, add readable writing, new symbols, extra figures, comparison boards or watermark.
Keep a VERY SHORT BROAD chin-to-neck transition meeting the original neckline and refit collar around its base: front cloth before neck, rear cloth behind it, coherent seam/fastening/contact shadow. No long yellow neck cylinder, floating collar, clipping, cream neck bib or invented garment opening. All subject surfaces and backing remain opaque. Exterior-only real transparency around the complete card silhouette. Preserve full 65:67 card canvas and do not crop the note.
FINAL REQUIRED CHECK: Correct the clearly wrong head direction and garment collar: Image 2 is nearly frontal with only a slight IMAGE-RIGHT turn; change Image 1 away from its current image-left three-quarter view. Keep both eyes almost equal in apparent size. Retain the source swept-back dark hair and visible eyebrow hair. Reproduce Image 2 blue-grey CLOSED HIGH tunic collar and central fastening, replacing the invented wide pointed folded collar. Serious closed mascot mouth, no added facial hair. Preserve existing opaque frame/backing/note and original crop.
Output alpha: genuine transparent RGBA ONLY OUTSIDE the complete original framed portrait silhouette. The photographic BACKING INSIDE the frame is a required OPAQUE surface: preserve its original background color and texture behind the character all the way to the inner frame rim. Never turn the gaps between frame and character into transparent holes or a window. Keep the actual frame angle and rim. Preserve an overlapping paper note, pin or other attachment ONLY when actually visible in this exact source; otherwise do not invent one. Do not invent a new backdrop outside the whole card. Retain source clothing, hair, headgear, lighting and crop at full generated resolution. All originally OPAQUE subject surfaces must remain FULLY OPAQUE (alpha 255): yellow head/body, hair, beard, dark or black clothing, coat lapels, collar, tie, buttons and decorations. Dark cloth is colored material, not transparent background. Never fade garment interiors into semi-transparent patches, holes, white haze or see-through fabric. Keep any genuine source outer-edge alpha falloff only at that actual exterior boundary; preserve actual source transparency rather than making the subject itself translucent.
